subject: Polity
description: State executive: Governor powers, appointment, CM, Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The Governor of a State is appointed by:

options.option_text: The Chief Minister of the state

questions.explanation: Article 155 — Governor appointed by the President of India; holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art 156). No fixed tenure in strict law; convention is 5 years. Governor must be a citizen of India, ≥35 years of age (Art 157).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Can a single person be appointed as Governor of TWO OR MORE states?
questions.explanation: 7th Constitutional Amendment (1956) allows one Governor to hold office of Governor of more than one state (Article 153 proviso). Common arrangement in NE states with smaller establishments.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CHIEF MINISTER of a state is:

options.option_text: Appointed by the Governor and must command majority in Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: CM is appointed by the Governor under Article 164. Usually the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly. If no clear majority, the Governor exercises discretion (often inviting the largest party or a pre-poll coalition first).
questions.subject: Polity

options.option_text: Reserving a bill for President's consideration (Article 200)
Removing the Chief Minister at will, without proof

questions.explanation: Article 200 — Governor can (a) assent, (b) withhold assent, (c) return a non-money bill for reconsideration, or (d) reserve for President's consideration. Reservation is MANDATORY if the bill endangers the High Court's position (Art 200 proviso). Sarkaria/Punchhi Commissions reviewed the Governor's discretionary powers.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 356 — 'President's Rule' in a state — is imposed on the recommendation of:

options.option_text: The Governor of the state (usually) + approval of the Union Cabinet
The Chief Minister of the state

questions.explanation: Article 356 — if the President (on the Governor's report or otherwise) is satisfied that the state's government cannot be run as per the Constitution, he can proclaim President's Rule. Proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 2 months. SR Bommai judgment (1994) laid down safeguards.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Legislative ASSEMBLY of a state has a minimum strength of:
questions.explanation: Article 170: minimum 60, maximum 500 members, directly elected. Exceptions by constitutional provision for smaller states: Sikkim, Mizoram, Goa (32), Arunachal Pradesh (60). Nagaland has 60; Manipur 60.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a discretionary power of the Governor in the usual sense?

options.option_text: Appointing the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority
Dismissing the Council of Ministers when it has lost majority
Reserving certain bills for the President's consideration
Nominating members to the Legislative Assembly without restriction

questions.explanation: Governors may nominate only one Anglo-Indian member to the Assembly (104th Amendment abolished this for Parliament; state-wise varies). Nomination to Legislative COUNCIL is partly by the Governor. But 'without restriction' is false.
